records.title: Contextual Regulation of the Kynurenine Pathway and Its Relevance for Personalized Psychiatry.

I have literature support for the neuroactive claim. I now have everything needed to revise the narrative — fixing the three unsupported claims, rephrasing to match confirmed pathway names from the enrichment, and adding the required Limitations paragraph.

**Revised Narrative:**

The most strongly enriched pathway across the differentially-abundant metabolites is **Tryptophan metabolism** (KEGG map00380; FDR = 0.0, fold-enrichment ≈ 625×). Five of the eight input compounds — L-tryptophan (C00078), serotonin (C00780), melatonin (C01598), 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (C00632), and quinolinic acid (C03722) — are annotated members of this pathway, making it the unambiguous biological driver of the observed metabolomic shift.

The strongest driver compounds are **quinolinic acid** (C03722) and **3-hydroxyanthranilic acid** (C00632), both confirmed KEGG members of Tryptophan metabolism. The neuroactive character of these metabolites in the context of tryptophan catabolism is supported by literature (PMID 41745408; PMID 41015495). **L-Tryptophan** (C00078) is the canonical entry point; a directed KEGG reaction path of four hops (L-tryptophan → N-formyl-L-kynurenine → L-kynurenine → 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid) confirms that the substrate sits upstream of 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid along the kynurenine pathway, consistent with a treatment-induced activation of tryptophan catabolism rather than simple accumulation.

The simultaneous elevation of **serotonin** and **melatonin** points to concurrent activation of the indoleamine branch. Melatonin, serotonin, and quinolinic acid are also jointly annotated in the WikiPathways "ADHD and autism (ASD) pathways" entry, hinting at neuropsychiatric-relevant pathway co-regulation. **4-Hydroxy-2-oxoglutaric acid** (C01127) is annotated in Glyoxylate and dicarboxylate metabolism (KEGG map00630), and the presence of **O-phosphoethanolamine** (C00346), a glycerophospholipid metabolism intermediate, suggests broader metabolic re-wiring that extends beyond the tryptophan axis, consistent with the high fold-enrichment of the broad "Biochemical pathways: part I" WikiPathways hit.

The convergence of the kynurenine arm toward quinolinic acid — a known NMDA receptor agonist and NAD⁺ biosynthetic precursor — implies that the treatment drives tryptophan flux toward neuroactive and energy-metabolite outputs. Elevated quinolinic acid and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid have been independently linked to oxidative stress and excitotoxicity in neurological disease contexts (PMID 41745408).

**Limitations:** Three input metabolites — 3-methyladenine (C00913), O-phosphoethanolamine (C00346), and 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutaric acid (C01127) — did not contribute to the top-ranked Tryptophan metabolism enrichment and may reflect off-target pathway perturbations or indirect effects not captured by the current KEGG annotation set.

I retract that parenthetical. For [c018], I replace the speculative treatment-mechanism claim with literature-grounded kynurenine-pathway language (PMID 41745408 already in hand). For [c035], the off-target perturbations sentence is unsupported by any database result and must be dropped entirely. The "Limitations" paragraph was itself new content — not a revision of an existing claim — so I remove it per Phase A2 Rule 3.
